test_cases.name: Statistically airtight, economically trivial
test_cases.rule_tested: Rule 1 -- stat significance is not business significance
test_cases.trap: Causal validity and statistical evidence both look excellent. A naive reviewer pattern-matches 'strong stats = SCALE' without separately weighing the thin economic margin.
test_cases.expected_correct_behavior: Recommendation should NOT be a clean SCALE. Economic attractiveness should be flagged as marginal/uncertain despite strong causal+statistical ratings -- the three axes must be rated independently.

bootstrap_ci_95.measures: within-unit week-to-week noise, cross-validated against a large donor pool

projected_extrapolation.key_assumption: flat retention curve, minimal extrapolation risk

test_cases.name: Structurally underpowered, misread as 'no effect'
test_cases.rule_tested: Rule 2 -- not significant is not no effect
test_cases.trap: Only 5 units total, so the best possible p-value is 1/5 = 0.20. A naive reviewer reads p=0.20 as 'no effect' and recommends DO NOT SCALE.
test_cases.expected_correct_behavior: Must explicitly name the structural power ceiling (1/placebo_pool_size) and avoid concluding 'no effect'. Recommendation should lean toward GATHER MORE EVIDENCE, not DO NOT SCALE.

bootstrap_ci_95.measures: within-unit week-to-week noise only, does not resolve cross-unit placebo uncertainty

projected_extrapolation.key_assumption: constant decay rate extrapolated to 52 weeks

test_cases.name: The iCAC/CLV conflation trap
test_cases.rule_tested: Rule 3 -- iCAC and CLV answer different questions
test_cases.trap: A significant retention gap is present. A naive reviewer writes something like 'the retention gap drove iCAC up' -- iCAC is not a function of retention at all.
test_cases.expected_correct_behavior: Must NOT attribute any change in iCAC to the retention finding. Must instead frame the retention gap purely as a threat to CLV/contribution/projected economics.

secondary_finding.description: week-4 retention, treatment cohorts vs. time-matched pre-treatment cohorts

projected_extrapolation.key_assumption: constant decay rate extrapolated to 52 weeks, despite the observed retention gap

test_cases.name: Observed floor fails, only the projection clears breakeven
test_cases.rule_tested: Rule 4 -- report observed vs. projected separately, always
test_cases.trap: The only confirmed number (observed_floor) is below breakeven. A naive reviewer leads with the flattering projected number and calls the deal ATTRACTIVE.
test_cases.expected_correct_behavior: Economic attractiveness must be UNCERTAIN, not ATTRACTIVE. Must state plainly that confirmed data says no and only an unverified extrapolation says yes.

projected_extrapolation.key_assumption: constant decay rate from only 4 weeks of observed data, extrapolated to 52 weeks

test_cases.name: Excellent fit, but nobody documented why this city was chosen
test_cases.rule_tested: Rule 5 -- causal validity requires checking selection, not just fit
test_cases.trap: Pre-treatment RMSE is very tight and placebo rank is #1 of a large pool -- everything LOOKS statistically airtight. A naive reviewer rates causal_validity STRONG based on fit quality alone, missing that treatment_selection_documented is false.
test_cases.expected_correct_behavior: Causal validity must be capped at MODERATE, with the selection-bias risk named explicitly in key_risks -- regardless of how good the fit metrics look.

bootstrap_ci_95.measures: within-unit week-to-week noise, cross-validated against a large donor pool

projected_extrapolation.key_assumption: constant decay rate extrapolated to 52 weeks

test_cases.name: Tight CI vs. non-significant placebo -- the real NovaPay case
test_cases.rule_tested: Rule 6 -- when uncertainty measures disagree, report both
test_cases.trap: This IS your actual NovaPay result (see evidence_novapay_real.json) -- reused here deliberately, since your own project already contains this exact trap and there's no need to invent a synthetic copy. A naive reviewer either leads with the flattering tight CI and buries the p=0.167, or does the reverse and calls it 'no effect.'
test_cases.expected_correct_behavior: Must state both measures, explain what each one does and doesn't capture (within-unit noise vs. cross-unit validity), and not let one silently override the other.

test_cases.name: Impressive headline iROAS, deteriorating marginal quality
test_cases.rule_tested: Rule 1 + Rule 4 combined -- headline metric vs. underlying quality signal
test_cases.trap: The projected iROAS (4.2x) is eye-catching. A naive reviewer anchors on that single headline number and calls it ATTRACTIVE/SCALE, without noticing the observed floor is below breakeven AND there's a large, significant retention gap undermining the very extrapolation the projection depends on.
test_cases.expected_correct_behavior: Must connect the secondary_finding (retention gap) to why the projected_extrapolation is fragile, must flag observed_floor.above_breakeven=false, and must not rate this ATTRACTIVE on the strength of the projected number alone.

secondary_finding.description: week-4 retention, treatment cohorts vs. time-matched pre-treatment cohorts -- large gap, treatment cohorts retaining worse

projected_extrapolation.key_assumption: constant decay rate extrapolated to 52 weeks, DESPITE the observed retention gap suggesting decay may accelerate, not stay constant

test_cases.name: A genuinely clean win -- positive control
test_cases.rule_tested: Calibration check -- the reviewer must recognize real strength, not just hunt for flaws
test_cases.trap: This case has NO significant caveats. A poorly-tuned reviewer that's been over-trained on 'always find the catch' might reflexively hedge into GATHER MORE EVIDENCE even here, which is its own failure mode -- excessive caution parroting rules without judgment.
test_cases.expected_correct_behavior: Should confidently output SCALE / STRONG / STRONG / ATTRACTIVE. A reviewer that can't recognize genuinely strong evidence is as broken as one that can't catch weak evidence.

bootstrap_ci_95.measures: within-unit week-to-week noise, cross-validated against a large donor pool

projected_extrapolation.key_assumption: modest, well-supported decay assumption consistent with 16 weeks of observed data
